**ACCEPT** — PR #9470, reviewer of record: PM loop (QA wave #9296), session `session_01Ai9gUdihXjg7FumzsBNSSs`.

**⛔ Accepted, NOT landed.** Skills are ADR-class; the PR stays draft, unmerged, unqueued, awaiting the maintainer. The `ADR maintainer approval` check is red and that is the gate reporting this PR's true state — the only legitimate way to turn it green is a human approval, and I have recorded on the PR that I will not weaken, re-scope, exempt or re-run it. This card goes into the round report under **"awaiting a human merge"**, not under done.

## Both open questions answered

**Language — A confirmed, keep the Chinese.** The card drafted the guardrail in English; the runner wrote it in Chinese and flagged the deviation rather than making it silently. It is right, and for the reason it gives: every other Guardrail bullet in that file is Chinese, and the card itself asked for 「the same register as 不伪造覆盖」. An English block would read as an imported quotation rather than a rule of the file — and a guardrail that reads like a citation is one a runner skims. Substance was preserved element for element.

**RUNNER carve-out — A confirmed**, and already in hand. Filed as **#9471** (the runner independently filed #9472; closed as duplicate, and the duplicate is my fault — I filed while it was still running and about to file it itself). B was never viable: leaving a one-sided guarantee on a rule whose failure mode is publishing a working exploit is exactly the incident this wave produced. C would have dragged `docs/qa/**` into an ADR-class review it does not need.

## What raises this above a competent execution

**It sharpened the diagnosis the card was built on.** I wrote that `checklist-test` was *silent* on access-control disclosure. It is not silent — §4 **requires** 「每个 `fail` 一条复现规则」 in the public run issue, and RUNNER rule 2 backs that unconditionally. So a runner following the skill faithfully is **instructed** to publish the reproduction. That is what happened in this wave: the runner did not deviate, it obeyed. An omission would have been fixable by addition; an active instruction had to be **named and overridden**, which is what the guardrail now does. The card would have produced a weaker fix.

**It verified rather than transcribed.** All six premises checked against the current files first — including one card error (the text sits at the end of §1, not §2). Entry 6 was confirmed three independent ways (the filter compares `App.name`; the pin asserts a non-match returns **200 with an empty list**, not 404; `adr-0048-app-split.test.ts` shows `com.objectstack.setup` is the *package* id of the app named `setup`) rather than on the card's say-so. It also explains *why* the error survived: the `?id=` line sat directly beneath `/_console/apps/` examples that legitimately do use package-shaped ids — two addressing schemes one line apart — so the fix names the distinction instead of only swapping a placeholder.

**It kept the rules durable.** Entries 2 and 3 state proportions and decision rules, not this wave's absolute counts — after a runbook in this same wave had to be corrected for baking in a millisecond figure measured on one loaded container.

**It respected a ceiling that does not exist.** `check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` does not cover these three files; the runner held to the discipline anyway rather than treating the absent ceiling as headroom, and filed **#9473** because the script's header claims a coverage it does not have. Treating an unenforced invariant as binding is the behaviour this repo is built around.

Line counts: checklist-test 131→163, checklist-author 55→61, dogfood-verification 142→148. Diff +47/−3 across exactly three files; nothing under `docs/qa/**` or `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/**`.
